buildSteps.title: Define the function
buildSteps.detail: Specify exactly what molecule or behaviour is wanted, and pick a chassis with the right metabolism and safety profile.

buildSteps.title: Design the DNA
buildSteps.detail: Software proposes gene sequences, promoters and copy numbers; the code is adjusted for the host's preferred codons and tuned so the pathway is not toxic.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the DNA
buildSteps.detail: Short oligonucleotides are built chemically, then stitched into genes or larger constructs. Synthesis cost has fallen steeply, which is what makes routine design possible.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and edit the genome
buildSteps.detail: Constructs are delivered into cells and either carried on a plasmid or written into the chromosome with editing enzymes. For a fully synthetic cell, an entire genome is assembled and transplanted into an emptied cell.

buildSteps.title: Screen and select
buildSteps.detail: Thousands of variants are tested in parallel for output; reporters and selection markers let the productive ones survive.

buildSteps.title: Iterate
buildSteps.detail: The design-build-test-learn cycle repeats, often with laboratory evolution, until yield, growth and stability are acceptable.

buildSteps.title: Scale up fermentation
buildSteps.detail: The winning strain is grown in progressively larger sterile bioreactors, with feed, oxygen, temperature and pH controlled.

buildSteps.title: Recover and purify
buildSteps.detail: Cells are separated and the product is extracted, purified and formulated to pharmaceutical or industrial grade.

buildSteps.title: Contain and regulate
buildSteps.detail: Engineered safeguards and waste handling are validated, and the product or organism is approved by the relevant regulator.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap, accurate DNA synthesis and sequencing
prerequisites.why: design is only practical if genes can be ordered and verified routinely.
CRISPR-based tools let specific changes be made without leaving scars.

prerequisites.tech: Predictive models of gene circuits and metabolism
prerequisites.why: simple pathways work, but whole-cell behaviour is still largely learned by trial and error.
done for a very small bacterial genome; not yet a general engineering method.
organisms released or used at scale must not survive or spread outside their intended setting.
many engineered products still cost more than the petrochemical equivalent.

pathway.milestone: engineered microbes making medicines, enzymes and food ingredients at industrial scale
pathway.unlocks: proven fermentation plants and regulatory experience.

pathway.milestone: living cell therapies — engineered immune cells already approved, engineered bacteria for gut disease in trials
pathway.unlocks: treatments that sense and respond inside the body.

pathway.milestone: minimal-genome and cell-free chassis with standardised parts
pathway.unlocks: faster, more predictable design and lower containment risk.

pathway.milestone: programmable organisms for materials, waste treatment or sensing, with built-in kill switches
pathway.unlocks: biology as a general manufacturing and environmental technology.
